author: Mark Atwood
text: DECISION 2026-05-12 (Mark, interactive): A2) Per-check, runtime-enumerated. Bridge crate exposes enumerate_lints() returning Vec<ZlintLintInfo> (metadata for every check zlint knows about) plus run_on_cert(cert) -> Vec<(CheckId, Verdict)> with per-cert result caching. Adapter creates dynamic Lint impls -- one per zlint check, each carrying (check_id, Arc<ZlintBridge>) -- that read from the bridge's per-cert cache. ~700 Lint instances total; subprocess cost is per-cert (paid once and cached), NOT per-Lint. RATIONALE: (1) Maps cleanly to existing Lint trait shape (one rule = one result). (2) Per-check granularity is framework-shaped; consumers compose their own profile by selecting Lint IDs. Umbrella would force accept-all-per-family or drop-down-to-zlint-args. (3) Reporting clarity: workspace Finding cleanly identifies which zlint check fired. (4) Runtime enumeration aligns with constraint 'Mark never transcribes someone else's policy' -- new zlint check upstream propagates automatically. (5) Per-cert subprocess cost amortizes correctly across the 700 Lint reads thanks to bridge caching (matches non-negotiable #6 cache-friendliness). CASCADE: PKIX-jy95.7 (pkix-zlint-bridge epic) gains design constraint -- bridge must expose enumerate_lints() + cached run_on_cert(). Likely same A2 pattern for PKIX-jy95.8 (pkix-pkilint-bridge) but that's an independent decision (pkilint's lint organization differs); marked in .8 description. CHILDREN STILL OPEN: .2 (severity mapping), .3 (batch shape), .4 (error handling) all still apply but their answers are now scoped to per-check Verdict shape, not umbrella shape.
